purpose: Extend the collection envelope the generated business surface already proves — items beside an opaque signed continuation cursor with bounded page sizes and stable ordering — to every management collection, so a native client can read large sites without unbounded lists or invented totals. The audited content list is capped at a flat 100 records without continuation, and menu, user and job lists are unpaginated or limit-only; none of these has a bounded-read contract today.

collections.title: Generated business browse and search
collections.observed_behavior: Opaque HMAC-signed keyset cursor, page size 1 to 200 with default 50, closed bounded query grammar, items with next_cursor and bounded aggregates.

collections.title: Business record history
collections.observed_behavior: Bounded revision window read with a limit and version continuation.

collections.title: Content list
collections.observed_behavior: Flat 100-record cap without continuation, search, filter or declared ordering.

collections.title: Menu and menu item lists
collections.observed_behavior: Unpaginated lists without a declared bound.

collections.title: User, role and token lists
collections.observed_behavior: Unpaginated lists without a declared bound; token lists never contain token material.

security_invariants: Cursors are opaque and integrity-protected; a client never decodes, edits or fabricates one, and a tampered cursor is refused.
A cursor is bound to its collection, site and authorization context; it is never honored for another caller or context.
Continuation never widens disclosure: every page re-applies current row and field policy, so revoked visibility disappears mid-iteration.
Totals are never invented; a collection either declares an exact total or reports none.
Page size requests above the declared maximum are refused rather than silently clamped, so a client never mistakes a partial read for a complete one.
Stable ordering is declared per collection; a client never assumes insertion order.
